hens_rule_text: Up to 15 hens and 30 growing chicks per premises, only with a permit from the county health unit, and the coop must be at least 100 feet from any dwelling, which rules out most ordinary city lots.
permit_notes: City code requires a permit from the county health unit (Florida Department of Health in Miami-Dade) authorizing the premises for poultry before any chickens are kept.
setback_notes: Poultry pens or houses may not be less than 100 feet from any human dwelling. Birds may not run at large.
coop_rules: Pens kept free of odor and fly breeding; feed in rat-proof covered containers; droppings removed at least twice a week and bagged for garbage pickup.
zoning_notes: Section 6-1 also says it does not allow any use that violates city zoning. This applies to the City of Miami only; unincorporated Miami-Dade County bans chickens in single-family residential districts, and other cities in the county have their own rules.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Read the full text of Sec. 6-1 from a 2019 PDF copy of the code (Municode is region-blocked here) and matched it to search extracts; no later amendment was found. Some secondary sites claim a 15 or 20 foot setback, which conflicts with the code's 100 feet, so the code figure is used.
